questions.problem:
Which of the following probabilities could be approximated using the normal approximation of the binomial distribution?

I. The probability that a fair coin lands on tails $45$ times out of $80$ coin flips.

II. The probability of getting $4$ even numbers on $6$ rolls of a $6$-sided die.

III. The probability that a fair spinner with four regions, red, green, yellow, and blue, lands on green at least $27$ times out of $60$ spins.
questions.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Let's now examine each situation.

- In situation I, we have $n=80$ and $p=\frac{1}{2}.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =80\cdot 0.5 \\  & =40 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =80\cdot (1-0.5) \\  & =40 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation II, we have $n=6$ and $p=\frac{1}{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =6\cdot 0.5 \\  & =3 \\  & ≯5.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, we *cannot* use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation III, we have $n=60$ and $p=\frac{1}{4}.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =60\cdot 0.25 \\  & =15 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =60\cdot (1-0.25) \\  & =45 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼B(90,0.47),$ use the normal approximation to the binomial distribution to approximate $P(40\le X<50).$ Give your final answer to three decimal places. *Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$$\,0.09\,$
$\,-0.6\,$ $\,0.2514\,$ $\,0.2483\,$ $\,0.2451\,$
$\,-0.5\,$ $\,0.2843\,$ $\,0.2810\,$ $\,0.2776\,$
$\,-0.4\,$ $\,0.3192\,$ $\,0.3156\,$ $\,0.3121\,$
$z$$\,0.00\,$$\,0.01\,$$\,0.02\,$
$\,1.4\,$ $\,0.9192\,$ $\,0.9207\,$ $\,0.9222\,$
$\,1.5\,$ $\,0.9332\,$ $\,0.9345\,$ $\,0.9357\,$
$\,1.6\,$ $\,0.9452\,$ $\,0.9463\,$ $\,0.9474\,$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=90$ and $p=0.47.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =90\cdot 0.47 \\  & =42.3 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =90\cdot (1-0.47) \\  & =47.7 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(90)(0.47)=42.3
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(90)(0.47)(1-0.47)=22.419.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(42.3,22.419).$

Now, we can estimate the desired probability $P(40\le X<50).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(40\le X<50)=P(40\le X\le 49)≈P(39.5\le Y\le 49.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(39.5\le Y\le 49.5) & =P(\frac{39.5-42.3}{\sqrt{22.419}}\le Z\le \frac{49.5-42.3}{\sqrt{22.419}}) \\  & ≈P(-0.59\le Z\le 1.52) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.52)-P(Z<-0.59) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.52)-P(Z\le -0.59) \\  & =Φ(1.52)-Φ(-0.59) \\  & =0.9357-0.2776 \\  & =0.6581\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(40\le X<50)≈0.658.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.6587.$

I. The probability that a fair coin lands on tails $5$ times out of $8$ coin flips.

II. The probability of choosing $5$ men in a neighborhood with $40$ adults if the probability that a randomly selected adult is a man is $0.55.$

III. The probability that a golf player makes less than $3$ putts in $15$ shots at the same hole if the probability of making a putt in each shot is $0.3.$

- $n(1-p)>5,$

$$

$$

- In situation I, we have $n=8$ and $p=0.5.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =8\cdot 0.5 \\  & =4 \\  & ≯5.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, we *cannot* use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation II, we have $n=40$ and $p=0.55.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =40\cdot 0.55 \\  & =22 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =40\cdot (1-0.55) \\  & =18 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation III, we have $n=15$ and $p=0.3.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =15\cdot 0.3 \\  & =4.5 \\  & ≯5.\,\times \end{aligned}
